correctness.rationale: Exact face set has 162 nonempty members by two independent exhaustive enumerators. Matching of 78 pairs is checked on all 432 covering relations, and a full 162-vertex topological sort verifies acyclicity. One critical vertex and five critical two-faces prove integral wedge-five S2 by Forman. Signed fixed-face Lefschetz traces of all 24 S4 permutations agree by conjugacy class with trivial+sign+sign-twisted standard. Finite-group rational invariant transfer proves the quotient claim; code is included, not merely logs.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new claim neither follows by substitution into the two-size theorem nor by a functor-equivalence from the matching or Rips claims. Its nontrivial sign-twisted standard summand requires a distinct signed Lefschetz computation.

originality.rationale: Exact same-family, matching-complex and graph-metric published claims were examined at full RESULT level and compared by simplex definitions and theorem quantifiers. Engström and Barmak primary texts provide broad methods, not the tetrahedral S4-character calculation. Neither the m=5,6 result nor a different truncated tetrahedral simplicial functor implies the present m=4 integral homotopy and character. Bibliographic priority still has unindexed-work risk.
residual_risks: Equivalent S4-character or m=4 independence computation may exist in unindexed or unavailable literature; priority is not certified.
A homotopy wedge by itself would be a small-family example, but the exact rational S4-module is the additional unforced structural invariant.

value.rationale: Canonical 12-vertex Archimedean solid and the smallest 3D truncated-simplex graph; its independence complex equals a natural subdivided tetrahedron matching complex. The complete rational tetrahedral symmetry module contains an unexpected sign-twisted 3D constituent plus two 1D constituents, and yields a specific rational quotient invariant not implied by homotopy rank alone or previously known m=5,6 models. Natural finite structural classification, rather than arbitrary slice.
